steps: Black in bucket 1 = 20% of 10 = 2 kg.
Black in bucket 2 = 20% of 20 = 4 kg.
Total black = 6 kg in 30 kg, so 6 ÷ 30 = 20%.
Shortcut: mixing two shades of the same strength never changes the strength.

steps: Rewrite: Bebby boughb some bubber, bub bhe bubber was boo bibber, so she pub a libble gummy bo make bhe bibber bubber yummy.
Go word by word. For each word, count how many different letters repeat.
Most words repeat only one letter. "libble" repeats l and b; "yummy" repeats y and m: 2 each.
10 words × 1 + 2 words × 2 = 14.

steps: Plain cube: 8 vertices, 12 edges.
Cutting each corner replaces 1 vertex with 3 and adds 3 edges: 24 vertices, 36 edges.
Each notch adds a small triangle (3 vertices, 3 edges) plus its inner tip (1 vertex, 3 edges): +4 vertices, +6 edges per face.

Scan the figure in strips from left to right, and tally that shape only.
Repeat for each shape type. Note the totals.
The largest tally is 9 (official key).

steps: Count the rings carefully: there are 10 (alternately face-on and edge-on).
The first ring gives its full outer diameter: 5 cm.
Each next ring passes inside the previous one, so it adds only its inner diameter: 5 − 1 − 1 = 3 cm.

steps: Turn every unit into pixels. 1 pica = 16 px, so 1 inch = 6 × 16 = 96 px.
6 points = half a pica = 8 px. 2 inches = 192 px. 3 picas = 48 px.
8 pixels = 8 px. 25 mm = 1 inch = 96 px.

steps: If 5 is used, the number must end in 5, so it is odd and 2 cannot be a digit.
If 5 is not used, the digits include 2, so the number must be even. Test 372, 732, 237 and so on: none works for all digits.
So use 3, 5, 7 and end in 5: try 375 and 735.

steps: A sphere touches the middle of each face of its corner space.

The 6 face-centre cubes touch only edge cubes, not corners.
The 1 cube in the very centre is also safe: 6 + 1 = 7.

If no rotation works but a mirror image does, it is flipped.
Two shapes need a mirror: the answer is 2.

steps: A "pattern" is the design of the grip area: straight stripes, slanted stripes, chevrons and so on.
Ignore the angle and the position of each pen. Look only at the texture.
Make a small list of patterns and add each new one as you scan.
The list ends with 5 different patterns.
qs.trap: Counting the same pattern again when the pen points the other way. Rotate it in your mind first.

steps: Count the pieces in Q and in each option. A different count rules an option out at once.
Match the shapes and sizes: two large triangles, a square and so on.
Check the colours, if the pieces are coloured.
B and D can make Q; A and C cannot.

steps: A: true. "Righty tighty": caps and screws tighten clockwise.
B: false. Most taps turn ON anticlockwise and OFF clockwise.
C: true. Nuts loosen anticlockwise ("lefty loosey").
D: false. Seen from above the North Pole, the Earth turns anticlockwise (west to east).

Rule 2: an open (straight) belt keeps the direction; a crossed belt reverses it.
Chain: 1 › crossed belt › 2 (opposite) › mesh › 3 (same as 1) › mesh › 4 (opposite) › straight belt › 5 (opposite) › mesh › 6 (same as 1).

The official key accepts both Chhattisgarh (B) and Madhya Pradesh (D).

steps: A single wire is one path with exactly two free ends.
Trace each frame with your eye from one arm tip. Do you reach the other arm tip without a joint?
Twisted joints where two wires meet show more than one wire.
C and D trace as one continuous wire; A and B show extra joints.
qs.trap: Being fooled by double lines. A double line can be one wire bent back on itself.

steps: The three examples show the same 3 letters rearranged, with a bar marking the position.
The fourth symbol has six squares and no bar, so the rule does not decide one answer.
The official key marks all four options correct.
In the exam, any choice here scored. Do not spend long on puzzles like this.
qs.trap: Spending minutes on one puzzle. If a pattern will not settle, mark your best guess and move on.

steps: Choose two or three very clear shapes in each option: a spiral, a hook, a leaf.
Find each one in K, allowing for its position and turn.
One shape that is missing from K, or mirrored, rules the option out.
B and D contain shapes not found in K.
qs.trap: Checking only the largest shape. Small curls are where the differences usually hide.

steps: A: aperture. A wider opening (smaller f-number) gives a shallower focus.
B: subject distance. A closer subject, refocused, blurs the background more.
D: focal length. A longer lens gives a shallower focus.
C: shutter speed only changes how long light enters. It affects brightness and motion blur, not depth of field.

About the short top edge: a cylinder with a cone-shaped dent (B).
About the slanted edge: a spindle of two cones (A). All four are possible.

steps: The largest cube touches the sphere at its 8 corners.
So the cube's long (space) diagonal equals the sphere's diameter, 20 cm.
A cube of edge a has space diagonal a3.
a3 = 20, so a = 20/3 cm.

steps: Split the drawing into zones: head and hat, body, legs, and the second figure.
In each zone, count small triangles first, then triangles made of two or more parts.
Mark each triangle with a light tick as you count it.
The total across all zones is 27.
qs.trap: Counting only the small triangles. Larger triangles made from two pieces are the ones most people miss.

steps: Do not try to rotate the whole pattern. Pick one piece near a corner that is easy to recognise.
Rotate only that piece 45° anticlockwise and see where it should land.
Check a second piece to confirm.
Only option B matches both pieces.

steps: The four logos differ in small details: the position of the "India Post" text and the yellow lines.
In the real logo, the text "India Post" sits at the bottom right of the red block.
Look at stamps, letters or the India Post website to fix the logo in memory.
Option D is correct.
qs.trap: Choosing by the overall look. Logo questions test small details: text position, line count, alignment.

steps: Look for cubes: 343, 216, 125, 64, 27 are 7³, 6³, 5³, 4³, 3³.
Each term is a cube minus 2: 343 − 2 = 341 and so on.
Check with differences: 127, 91, 61, 37 fall by 36, 30, 24, so next 18. 37 − 18 = 19 and 25 − 19 = 6.

steps: Read each word backwards.
WOW, MADAM, CIVIC, ROTATOR, NOON, SAGAS and LEVEL all read the same: they are palindromes.
SOLO backwards is OLOS, so it is not a palindrome.
Option C is the odd one out.

steps: Compare the 1st and 3rd figures to see what changes in two steps.
Follow one black arrow and one white triangle separately: each turns by a fixed amount per step.
The missing figure must sit halfway between its neighbours.
Option C fits both the arrow turn and the triangle turn.
qs.trap: Tracking the whole figure at once. Follow one element, then confirm with a second.

steps: Look at letter features, not size: serifs (small feet), stroke contrast, letter width, the shape of "a", "g" and "t".
Group words that share all features.
Bold or larger text in the same design is the same font family.
The words fall into 5 groups.
qs.trap: Counting size or boldness changes as new fonts. Only a change in letter design counts.

qs.note: Nagaland holds it near Kohima from 1 to 10 December. The hornbill is a bird that appears in many Naga stories. Shillong is a city, not a government.
A wax model is covered in clay, the wax is melted out and molten metal is poured into the hollow. The Chola bronzes and Dhokra craft use it. Batik uses wax too, but as a dye resist.
Water finds the same level at both ends of a filled pipe. Mark the two water levels on the wall: they are exactly level. This is how masons check levels.
Cobra, krait and Russell's viper are three of India's "big four" venomous snakes. The rat snake is not venomous.
The first three are surface finishes that protect or colour a product. Drilling removes material to make a hole.

steps: First differences: 4, 7, 12, 20.
Second differences: 3, 5, 8. Each is the sum of the two before it (3 + 5 = 8).
Next second difference: 5 + 8 = 13. Next first difference: 20 + 13 = 33.

steps: The artist was Marcel Duchamp, and the 1919 work is called L.H.O.O.Q.
Dada artists mocked the art world and "serious" art after World War I.
Defacing a famous masterpiece was exactly the kind of joke Dada liked.
Pop Art came later (1950s) and Cubism was about form, not satire.

steps: Mango: long, narrow leaf with a pointed tip, often drooping (leaf 3).
Chikoo: glossy, oval, slightly pointed, darker green (leaf 4).
Guava: light green, oblong, with clear parallel veins (leaf 2).
Jackfruit: large, thick, dark and broad (leaf 1).
qs.trap: Guessing from leaf size alone. Look at vein pattern, tip shape and gloss.

steps: Mango is a soft hardwood used for cheap furniture.
Teak is valued for durability and oil content more than hardness.
Rosewood is very dense, heavy and hard, used for fine furniture and instruments.
The official key gives rosewood.
qs.trap: Confusing durability with hardness. Teak lasts long outdoors, but rosewood is harder.

steps: A hex code has three pairs: red, green, blue. Equal pairs mean a grey.
CC in hex = 12 × 16 + 12 = 204, out of a maximum of 255 (FF).
204 ÷ 255 = 0.8, so it is 80% of the way to white.
That is light grey: 80% white, 20% black.

steps: At 2 the tip is a little above the centre. At 3 it is level with the centre.
It drops to its lowest at 6, then rises back to centre level at 9.
Add the steady movement to the right: the path dips down and rises again.
It ends lower than it started (9 is level, 2 is above). That is option A.
qs.trap: Tracing the minute hand. The hour hand moves only 7 hours here: just over half a turn.

steps: The first reflection turns the word upside down; letters keep their left-right order.
The second reflection mirrors it left to right.
Two reflections at right angles equal one half-turn (180° rotation).
So the word reads upside down and backwards, letter by letter: option B.

Slanted bar (4 sides › 6) and the two quarter discs do not pass. Answer: 3.
